population_estimates.note: Chan Chan resident population estimate; total kingdom likely ~600,000.

description: Late-Intermediate Period kingdom occupying the north coast of present-day Peru, with its capital at Chan Chan, a planned earthen-walled city of some twelve square kilometres, the largest pre-Columbian urban centre in the Americas before Tenochtitlan. Chimor's coastal-irrigation polity controlled a thousand-kilometre stretch from Tumbes south to the Lima area until the late-fifteenth-century Inca conquest under Tupac Inca Yupanqui absorbed it into Tawantinsuyu.

temporal.notes: North-coast Peruvian kingdom centred on Chan Chan; absorbed by the Inca conquest under Tupac Inca Yupanqui around 1470.

geographic.notes: Centroid set at Chan Chan near modern Trujillo.

lifecycle_phases.description: Early Chimor consolidation around Chan Chan after collapse of Moche.
Hydraulic expansion across north-coast valleys; Chan Chan reaches monumental form.
Late Chimor reaches Tumbes in the north; Inca conquest c. 1470 ends independent rule.

rise_factors.description: Engineered canals linking the Moche, Chicama, and Jequetepeque valleys irrigated tens of thousands of hectares of coastal desert.
Ciudadela compound system, each king built a new walled palace, sealed at death, gave continuity to a dynastic-administrative apparatus.

decline_factors.description: Topa Inca Yupanqui's c. 1470 conquest absorbed Chimor into Tawantinsuyu, ending independent rule.
